$comment: Hard gate for config/litellm-proxy.yaml (fleet-ops#8653). Nish 2026-09-28: no benching unless he says so. A failed row is never taken out of rotation: no bench list. Row cooldown_time: <=900 s is for ordinary transients. Values over 900 s, up to the 86400 s cap, are reserved for rows with a named, self-refilling wall (a daily or monthly quota that outlasts 900 s) - the row stays live, parked, and re-probes itself; each such row cites its issue in a comment (fleet-ops#8398/#9075). A row on openrouter.ai/api/v1 must set model_info.allowed_fails_policy.RateLimitErrorAllowedFails: 0, because its 429s are OpenRouter's named daily free-tier wall and the row has to park on the first one (fleet-ops#9248). Router-level cooldown_time holds a failed row for at most 60 s. router_settings.redis_url is required: session_affinity pins live in the Router cache, and without Redis each of the proxy's 2 worker processes keeps its own pin, so a session flips between rows with no failure (fleet-ops#9015). LiteLLM v1.98.0 never reads a redis_url under general_settings.

judgePaidRow.$comment: fleet-ops#9374: the paid row, on the Token Plan's own numbers. rpm and max_parallel_requests are what the plan allows (3 per minute, 3 at once); neither was raised when the row became the judge primary, and raising either is a deliberate change with its own issue, not an edit to this file. model and api_base pin the seat, so a judge row cannot point the order-1 rung at another provider.

judgeFallbackRow.$comment: fleet-ops#9374: whatever else answers a judge call answers after the paid row, never beside it, and it is an OpenCode Go row: the paid row duplicated as an order-2 fallback would pass a count-only rule and quietly keep judge traffic on the one seat the fallback exists to take off.

allOf.$comment: fleet-ops#9374: the judge group used to shuffle all three rows, so the paid Alibaba Token Plan seat answered 22 of 1,054 judge calls in 14 days to 2026-10-07 while both OpenCode Go rows carried the traffic - the same family the builders use, which memory grader-never-builder-family forbids for the grader. Exactly three judge rows: one paid row on order 1 and the two fallbacks on order 2. LiteLLM v1.98.0 keeps only the lowest order group (utils._get_order_filtered_deployments) and applies that filter after the cooldown filter (router.py), so the paid row answers every judge call and the pair answers while it is cooled - measured 200/200 and 200/100 on the real Router, with every row back on order 1 spreading 30/40/30. A fourth judge row, a third order-1 row, or the fallbacks on order 1 all fail here.
the two named OpenCode Go fallback rows, each present exactly once and on order 2, so a fourth judge row cannot arrive by renaming or by copying one of them

fleet-ops#9248: a row on openrouter.ai/api/v1 is metered by OpenRouter's free-tier DAILY quota, so its RateLimitError must park the row on the first failure. Without RateLimitErrorAllowedFails the router-level default of 1 needs a second 429, and the wall leaks to the caller: 4 of 30 parallel worker-capable calls on 2026-10-04.
